hypotheses.statement: A rollout to ticketbooking:1.1 (revision 2) was initiated and is stalling: the single new pod is stuck in ContainerCreating while the two revision-1 pods running ticketbooking:1.0 remain healthy. The change_cause field explicitly labels revision 2 as a regression.
hypotheses.confidence_reason: All signals converge: revision 2 has 0 ready replicas, the new pod is Pending/ContainerCreating, the deployment reports rollout_complete=false and healthy=false, and the health endpoint responds 200 serving version 1.0 — meaning traffic is still being served by the old pods.

contradicting_evidence: The pod is still in ContainerCreating (not CrashLoopBackOff or ImagePullBackOff), so it is theoretically possible the image pull is just slow rather than permanently broken — however the change_cause label 'regression' strongly indicates intentional acknowledgement of a bad release

root_cause.statement: Revision 2 (ticketbooking:1.1) was deliberately labelled a regression at deploy time and is failing to produce ready pods, causing a stalled rolling update. Revision 1 (ticketbooking:1.0) is confirmed healthy with 2 ready replicas and a passing health check.

bob_analysis.dual_signal_note: The deployment's current image is ticketbooking:1.1 (revision 2, is_current=true) yet the health endpoint reports version='1.0' and healthy=true. These are not contradictory: the two surviving revision-1 pods are still serving traffic because the rolling update has not yet replaced them. The healthy signal reflects the old pods, not the new revision.
bob_analysis.reason: Human feedback required confirming a healthy revision exists before acting. Revision 1 is confirmed healthy: rollout_history shows ready_replicas=2, change_cause='Restore ticketbooking:1.0 (healthy)', and the live health endpoint independently confirms version 1.0 is serving HTTP 200. Rolling back to revision 1 terminates the stalled revision-2 pod and restores the deployment to its fully healthy prior state.
bob_analysis.risk_explanation: Revision 1 is already serving live traffic successfully (health check: 200, version=1.0). Rolling back re-pins the deployment to that known-good image. The only risk is a brief re-scheduling period if Kubernetes terminates and recreates pods, but two healthy pods are already up, satisfying MinimumReplicasAvailable throughout.
bob_analysis.blast_radius: Affects only the ticket-booking deployment in namespace opspilot. The Pending revision-2 pod (ticket-booking-596f87b86b-6zt8x) will be terminated; the two revision-1 pods are expected to remain running or be replaced by identical revision-1 pods to meet desired_replicas=3. No other workloads or namespaces are referenced in the evidence.
bob_analysis.expected_effect: The Pending ticketbooking:1.1 pod is removed; the deployment scales back to 3 ready replicas all running ticketbooking:1.0; workload conditions show Available=True and rollout_complete=true; the health endpoint continues to return HTTP 200 version=1.0.
